主要内容: On July 25, 2017, the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) issued an investigative report cautioning market participants about the regulatory implications of digital asset offerings. The report concluded that DAO tokens, a type of digital asset, were classified as securities and therefore subject to federal securities laws. The SEC emphasized that offers and sales of digital assets by 'virtual' organizations, such as those using blockchain or distributed ledger technology, may fall under U.S. securities regulations. The report highlighted that securities exchanges must register unless exempt, and that investors must receive proper disclosures. The investigation was conducted by the SEC's Distributed Ledger Technology Working Group (DLTWG), led by Valerie A. Szczepanik, with assistance from other divisions. The report serves as a resource for investors and underscores the regulatory scrutiny of digital assets. The SEC also warned about the risks associated with initial coin offerings (ICOs) and emphasized the importance of disclosure requirements and investor protections. The report stems from an inquiry into whether The DAO and associated entities violated securities laws by conducting unregistered offers and sales of DAO tokens in exchange for Ether, a virtual currency. The SEC decided not to bring charges but to caution the industry about the applicability of federal securities laws to all offerings, regardless of the technology used.
